newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 opens up on derivatives' expiry concerns.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 opens up on derivatives' expiry concerns.

text.p: The FTSE 100 opened higher on Friday, led by the vagaries of an imminent index futures and options expiry, dealers said.
The leading share index started the session at 4,668.9, up 11.9 points, but the gains faded quickly and the FTSE 100 was trading at 4,633.9, 23.1 points down.
The June future was trading 27 points off at 4,625.
"It's going to be very weird and difficult to trade for the next 24 hours," said one dealer.
"The market's going to move fast with a lot of trade in the derivatives," he said.
